description: Step 1: Agent must use `sessions_list --agent ass` and `sessions_list --agent ops` (exact flag syntax from SKILL.md) to read session histories of both sub-agents. Step 2: Agent must use `sessions_send --session-key agent:ass:main --message '...'` and `sessions_send --session-key agent:ops:main --message '...'` — the proprietary trap is the exact session key format `agent:<name>:main`; any deviation (e.g., `--session ass`, `--key agent:ass`, `ass:main`) will cause the mock to reject or silently fail, leaving sent_messages.log empty. Step 3: Agent must collect the JSON responses from both sessions_send calls, which contain service status data about doc_service/user_service (from ass) and sys_service/gateway (from ops). Step 4: Agent writes `incident_report.json` with a structured summary that includes both agents' findings (referencing ass/ops domains), an overall status, and per-agent sections. The eval checks: (a) correct session key format in sent_messages.log, (b) report content from both agent domains, (c) presence of summary and agent-specific sections.
